clue.text: Additional comment recalled at this point in class

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back in the opposite order

blocks.note: a postscript, abbreviated PS, is a comment added at the end of a letter
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: A teacher remembers an extra remark made at this moment in the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' is not a school class here but a social or professional level.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphere and class both mean a social rank or field of activity, as in 'moving in different spheres'.

clue.text: Promise to repay accepted by a class outraged about lustful behaviour

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, 'concerning lust', matching the adjective

indicators.note: outraged suggests things thrown into turmoil, so the letters are disturbed
something accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the mixed letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
an IOU is a written promise to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A class of pupils lends money and is scandalised about some lewd conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixed letters of 'a class' wrap round IOU. 'About' belongs to the definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacious describes material dealing with sex in an indecent, titillating way.

clue.text: Contain our group in garden

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following verb

blocks.note: to hoe is to garden, weeding with a hoe
us refers to our group

explanation.surface: Keep our party inside the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To house something is to hold or accommodate it, as a case contains a mechanism.

clue.text: Actor Montalban, bit of a character in Brazilian city

indicators.note: in means placed inside the city's name

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro
someone who is a bit of a character is a card, an amusing eccentric

explanation.surface: A film actor, something of an eccentric, turns up in Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricardo Montalban was the Mexican-born star of Fantasy Island and Star Trek II, his first name being the answer.

clue.text: Family document about good party with royal associations?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the document wraps round what follows

blocks.note: kin are relatives
G is the abbreviation for good
a do is a party
MS is short for manuscript

explanation.surface: A family paper on a good party with links to royalty, perhaps a society diary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: kingdoms are what royals are associated with, the realms they rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a realm ruled by a monarch, so kingdoms are territories tied to royalty.

clue.text: Metal I note, dull, found around uranium

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the dull word encloses the element symbol

blocks.note: taken as written
n is the abbreviation for note, as in dictionaries
dim means dull or faint
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemist notes a dull metal found near uranium ore.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside DIM, after I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Indium is a soft silvery chemical element, a metal used in touchscreens.

clue.text: French holiday home containing rendered stone

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the holiday home wraps round the next word

blocks.note: a gîte is a French holiday cottage
rendered fat is melted down, and melted colours or wax are said to have run

explanation.surface: A French cottage built of plastered stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendered stone' reads as plastered masonry, but 'rendered' is wordplay and 'stone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock used in building.

clue.text: Left in one large reconstructed part of cell

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something left inside a big rebuilt section of a prison block.
explanation.walkthrough: L is placed among the letters of 'one large' and all are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: An organelle is a specialised structure within a living cell, such as a mitochondrion.

clue.text: Work out without others? Very into that

indicators.note: into means going inside the word that follows

blocks.note: sole means alone, with no others
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Can you figure it out on your own? You're really into that.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a puzzle is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Meal encapsulating a flat opening event?

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as in a capsule, so the meal goes round the next item

blocks.note: lunch is a midday meal
taken as written
a pad is informal for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A lunch held to show off a new apartment, like a housewarming.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a launchpad is where a rocket's opening event, its launch, happens. Pad is informal for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A launchpad is the platform from which rockets lift off, figuratively a starting point for any venture.

clue.text: Member of Parliament importing very soft pelt

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the member takes the next item inside

blocks.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords, part of Parliament
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: An MP brings in a very soft animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of Parliament' suggests MP, but a peer in the Lords is equally a member. 'Pelt' looks like a noun, a fur, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper someone is to bombard them with many small missiles, the same as to pelt.

clue.text: Theatrical sponsor: a new stage backed

indicators.note: backed suggests going backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A new theatre production gets financial backing from a sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' and 'backed' both sound theatrical, but the stage is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang an angel is a private investor who finances a show.

clue.text: Entertainment from American singer with a repeat for English

indicators.note: a repeat means one letter appears a second time, slotted in beside its twin

blocks.note: Cher is the American singer and actress
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An evening of entertainment provided by an American singer who performs an encore for English fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Cher's name already contains an E; doubling it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer in the older sense means food, drink and hospitality, as in 'good cheer' laid on for guests.

clue.text: Uncommonly nice and pure about a bit of rumpy-pumpy? This is being just the opposite

definitions.text: This is being just the opposite

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests an unusual form, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged words go round the extra letter

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to be mixed
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone innocent and wholesome is set beside a bit of sexual romping, and is the reverse of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at 'nice and pure': prurience is their opposite. Rumpy-pumpy is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurience is an excessive interest in sexual matters, the opposite of being chaste and wholesome.

clue.text: Caught within six deliveries? Quick assessment required

indicators.note: within means placed inside the following phrase

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes a batsman caught out inside one over, demanding a quick verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside ONE, then OVER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a rapid inspection or glance to size something up.

clue.text: Constant of the people to accept sopranos in such music?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the word for of the people goes round the singers

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
laical means lay, belonging to the ordinary people rather than clergy
S is the abbreviation for soprano, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Is music that steadily takes in sopranos the kind sung for the people?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: sopranos sing in classical music. Laical is a rare word for lay, not clerical.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical music is the serious Western art tradition in which sopranos perform opera and oratorio.

clue.text: Wild situation with heartless devil seen in torchlight

indicators.note: without a heart, so the interior letters are removed and only the ends remain
seen in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: the word with its middle letters taken out
a torch gives a beam of light

explanation.surface: A chaotic scene in which a soulless demon appears in the glow of a torch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torchlight' is one word but stands for the light a torch casts, not the torch itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a London asylum, means uproar and confusion.

clue.text: A lot of nasty crime done - by me?

definitions.text: A lot of nasty crime done - by me?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes
done in the sense of done over, wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain confesses to plenty of horrible offences.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the speaker who commits nasty crimes is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who commits crimes.

clue.text: Curtailment of complicated dispute to distress

indicators.note: curtailing cuts off the tail, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: hard means complicated; the word loses its last letter
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Cutting short a complex argument may cause pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow someone is to torment or upset them deeply, as in a harrowing experience.

clue.text: Biscuits etc seen aboard ship a good deal

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so these go inside the ship abbreviation

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship
tack, or hardtack, is the hard biscuit eaten by sailors

explanation.surface: Plenty of biscuits and other food stowed on a ship for a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardtack was the dry biscuit of sailors' rations, so the nautical surface hides a real ship's biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks is informal for a large amount, as in 'stacks of money'.

clue.text: Currently blocking chesspiece, showing cunning

indicators.note: something blocking another sits in its middle, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the king is a chess piece
now means at present

explanation.surface: A chess player cleverly obstructs a piece right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A knowing look suggests shrewd, sly awareness, the same as cunning.

clue.text: Student's beset by evil, being blunt

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so the student goes inside

blocks.note: badness is evil or wickedness
L, the learner plate, stands for a student; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A student is under attack by wickedness, a grim moral tale.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside BADNESS after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald statement is plain and direct, so baldness is the quality of bluntness.

clue.text: Interfere with day, getting purist upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stickler is upset when someone meddles with their day.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrupt is to interrupt or disturb something's normal course.

clue.text: Attack joke about old church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joke goes round the next letter

blocks.note: a pun is a wordplay joke
O is the abbreviation for old
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out at a joke made at the expense of an ancient church.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly on prey, a sudden attack.

clue.text: Make bad comments about food prepared for us

blocks.note: a dish is a prepared item of food
on means arranged or under way, as in 'dinner is on'
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a meal that was cooked for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests being rude about the cooking, but the first four words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishonour is to disgrace or show disrespect, as unfavourable remarks about someone do.

clue.text: Had to deal with getting up and coffee without the kick!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: to have faced a problem is to have had to deal with it

explanation.surface: Someone groggy on waking had to make do with weak coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is decaffeinated coffee, lacking the caffeine jolt.

clue.text: One using needle or pin, not end of stick

indicators.note: not means without, so one letter is taken away
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'stick'

blocks.note: a skewer is a long pin for holding meat
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone working with a needle or a pin, but not the tip of a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: K is removed from SKEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer, pronounced like 'sower', is a person who stitches with needle and thread.

clue.text: Trace of cork in Merlot perhaps producing pained expression

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next item

blocks.note: Merlot is a red wine
a trace means just the first letter

explanation.surface: Finding bits of cork in your red wine makes you grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: Corked wine is spoiled, so the surface's grimace is natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A wince is a brief grimace or flinch of pain.

clue.text: Desert plants have a role in Channel Islands

indicators.note: in means placed inside the islands' abbreviation

blocks.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: Plants usually found in deserts have a part to play in Jersey and Guernsey's gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulents typical of arid regions.

clue.text: Pacific island, genuine and raw, deposing King in rebellion

indicators.note: deposing a monarch removes them, so the royal letter is taken out
a rebellion overturns order, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An island nation in the Pacific, authentic and untamed, overthrows its king in a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: R is removed from RAW, leaving AW to mix with GENUINE.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is the large island north of Australia, the world's second biggest.

clue.text: I get food, gratis, coming in for nothing - it's a delicate arrangement

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these go inside the next word

blocks.note: free means costing nothing
taken as written
to lig is British slang for freeloading at parties for free food and drink

explanation.surface: A freeloader boasts of eating at no cost, calling it a delicate arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Lig is British slang for scrounging free food and drink at launches and parties; 'gratis' and 'for nothing' look like repetition but do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is fine ornamental metalwork of twisted wire, a delicate lacy pattern.

clue.text: Plant embedded in stone thoroughfare

indicators.note: embedded in means set firmly inside the following word

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
a tree is a plant

explanation.surface: A plant has taken root in a paved road.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, a thoroughfare lined with buildings.
